full_text_en:
Guangzhou Xianyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd. v. Guangdong Zhongda Zhongxin Investment Planning Co., Ltd., Guangzhou Yuanxing Real Estate Co., Ltd., and China Investment Group International Finance Co., Ltd. — dispute over equity transfer

【Ruling Summary】

I. Where one partner transfers its rights and obligations under a Chinese-foreign cooperative enterprise contract, and the transfer contract has not been submitted for approval by the approving authority after its formation, the validity of the contract shall be determined as not yet effective, rather than void.

II. Even if the transfer contract has not been approved, the obligation to "submit for approval" shall still be deemed to have arisen at the time the contract was formed; otherwise, a party may maliciously prevent the contract from becoming effective by willfully failing to handle or assist in handling the "submission for approval" procedures, which is contrary to the principle of good faith.

III. Article 8 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation (II) of Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides that where a party obligated to apply for approval procedures fails to do so in accordance with the law or the contract, the people's court may order the counterparty to handle the relevant procedures on its own, and the other party shall bear liability for damages for the expenses incurred and the actual losses suffered by the counterparty as a result. Accordingly, the people's court may also, upon the request of a party, order the obligor to perform the obligation of submitting the matter for approval by the approving authority.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2009) Min Shen Zi No. 1068

Retrial Applicant (Defendant at First Instance / Appellant at Second Instance): Guangdong Zhongda Zhongxin Investment Planning Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 409, No. 46 Zhongshan Ba Road, Liwan District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: He Shaoliu, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: Zhang Biao, lawyer of Guangdong Guodao Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Ke Yien, trainee lawyer of Guangdong Guodao Law Firm.

Retrial Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance / Appellee at Second Instance): Guangzhou Xianyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 01, 11/F, East Tower, Huapu Plaza, No. 13 Huaming Road, Tianhe District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Wen Kaiping, General Manager of the company.

Agent ad litem: An Bo, lawyer of Guangdong Shengchen Law Firm.

Agent ad litem: Feng Guobin, lawyer of Guangdong Shengchen Law Firm.

Original Defendant at First Instance / Appellee at Second Instance: Guangzhou Yuanxing Real Estate Co., Ltd., domiciled at Room 06, 11/F, Guangdong Shipping Building, No. 48 Baqi Erma Road, Yuexiu District, Guangzhou, Guangdong Province.

Legal Representative: Lin Bang, Chairman of the Board of the company.

Original Defendant at First Instance / Appellee at Second Instance: China Investment Group International Finance Co., Ltd. (CHINA INVESTMENT GROUP INT'L FINANCE LIMITED), domiciled at Room 1002, Eastern Commercial Centre, 397 Hennessy Road, Wan Chai, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.

Legal Representative: Xu Xianchi, Director of the company.

The retrial applicant, Guangdong Zhongda Zhongxin Investment Planning Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongxin Company), filed an application for retrial with this Court, dissatisfied with the civil judgment (2008) Yue Gao Fa Min Si Zhong Zi No. 323 rendered by the Guangdong High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of second instance) on March 10, 2009, in a dispute over equity (interest) transfer with the retrial respondent, Guangzhou Xianyuan Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Xianyuan Company), and the original defendants at first instance, Guangzhou Yuanxing Real Estate Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yuanxing Company) and China Investment Group International Finance Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Finance Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law to conduct the review, which has now been completed.

Xianyuan Company filed an action with the Guangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance), alleging: On January 9, 2007, Zhongxin Company and Finance Company won the bid for 100% of the capital contributions and interests of Yuanxing Company through an auction, and, under the witness of the Guangzhou Property Rights Exchange (hereinafter referred to as the Property Exchange), signed the "Contract for Transfer of Capital Contributions and Interests" with the original contributors of Yuanxing Company. After Zhongxin Company acquired the said interests, on April 28, 2007, it signed the "Contract for Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation of Guangzhou Yuanxing Real Estate Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract") with Xianyuan Company, stipulating that Zhongxin Company would transfer 28.5% of the equity it held in Yuanxing Company to Xianyuan Company, and that within three days after the completion of the transfer procedures between Zhongxin Company and the original shareholders of Yuanxing Company, the relevant industrial and commercial registration modification procedures would be handled; in case of delay, the liquidated damages would be 1% per day. After the contract was signed, Xianyuan Company paid the equity transfer price as agreed; the equity transfer procedures between Zhongxin Company and the original shareholders of Yuanxing Company were completed on July 24, 2007, but Zhongxin Company, despite repeated reminders from Xianyuan Company, failed to handle the equity modification procedures, causing serious economic losses to Xianyuan Company. Xianyuan Company requested the court to order: 1. Zhongxin Company, Yuanxing Company, and Finance Company to immediately handle the industrial and commercial registration modification procedures for transferring the 28.5% interest held by Zhongxin Company in Yuanxing Company to the name of Xianyuan Company; 2. Zhongxin Company to pay liquidated damages for delay at the rate of 1‰ per day until the date of completion of the industrial and commercial registration modification procedures (the amount of liquidated damages from July 28, 2007, tentatively calculated to November 27, 2007, being RMB 5.16 million); 3. Zhongxin Company to deliver for safekeeping to Xianyuan Company the relevant certificates and licenses of Yuanxing Company's real estate project, namely the original State-owned Land Use Certificate for the said real estate project.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

Zhongxin Company was formerly named "Guangdong Zhongda Zhongqian Investment Planning Co., Ltd." (hereinafter referred to as Zhongqian Company), and changed to its current name upon approval by the Guangdong Provincial Administration for Industry and Commerce on January 26, 2007. Yuanxing Company is a Sino-foreign (Hong Kong) cooperative real estate development project company registered in Guangzhou on August 18, 1993, organized as a limited liability company, with its business scope including "development, construction, sale, leasing, and management of self-built commercial buildings on the land parcels at No. 19-49 Dezheng South Road and No. 22-28 Fuxing Street" (hereinafter referred to as the disputed real estate project). At the time of its establishment, the Chinese and foreign cooperative parties were Guangzhou Erqing Real Estate Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Erqing Real Estate) and Hong Kong Zhuokang Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hong Kong Zhuokang), respectively.

On January 9, 2007, Erqing Real Estate (Party A), Hong Kong Zhuokang (Party B), Zhongqian Company (Party C), and Finance Company (Party D), under the witness of the Property Exchange, signed a "Contract for Transfer of Capital Contributions and Interests." The contract stated: Whereas Party A, as the Chinese contributor, and Party B, as the foreign contributor, based on their registered capital, land use rights, and other cooperative conditions, respectively obtained the right to distribute building area in the "Global Tower" project of the target company (Yuanxing Company) at 40% for Party A and 60% for Party B after completion; Parties C and D are willing to acquire all of the capital contributions and interests of Parties A and B in the target company and agree to perform their obligations in accordance with the law and the contract; the subject matter of the transfer is all of the capital contributions and interests of the Chinese and foreign cooperative parties in Yuanxing Company and all of their rights and obligations under Yuanxing Company's articles of association, cooperation contract, and corresponding amendment documents; the transfer price is the amount bid by Parties C and D, namely RMB 85 million, which Parties C and D agree to pay in full within 20 days after signing the contract, with 50% thereof (RMB 42.5 million) to be paid within 10 days after signing; to ensure the smooth progress of the transaction, the four parties entrust the Property Exchange to supervise and settle the transaction funds; Parties C and D shall transfer the payable amount into the Property Exchange's supervision account within the agreed time; in addition to the transfer price, Parties C and D shall also assume the target company's debts of RMB 2.5 million and pay the archive deposit and municipal management fees previously advanced by Party B for the target company, totaling RMB 768,000; during the period from the enterprise handover date (i.e., within 3 working days after Parties C and D pay the full amount, the Property Exchange organizes the four parties to handle the enterprise handover procedures) to the equity delivery date (i.e., the date when the target company's contributors are changed in the industrial and commercial registration authority), the transferee is responsible for the management and safety of the target company, and the target company's official seals (including but not limited to official seal, contract seal, and financial seal) shall be temporarily held by the Property Exchange; within 3 working days from the equity delivery date, the Property Exchange and Parties A and B shall end their supervision of the target company and hand over the seals and certificates to Parties C and D. In addition, the contract also stipulated other conditions of the transfer, employee placement, assets, claims, debts, and owner's equity.

On April 28, 2007, Zhongqian Company (Party A, as the equity transferor), Xianyuan Company (Party B, as the equity transferee), and Finance Company (Party C, as the project cooperation party) jointly signed the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract," stating: Party A and Party C lawfully obtained through the Property Exchange in a public auction 100% of the equity of Yuanxing Company, with Party A holding 40% equity and Party C holding 60% equity; the auction subject amount was RMB 85 million; Party A and Party C jointly paid RMB 42.8 million of the auction price, leaving a funding gap of RMB 45.918 million; after consultation, the three parties agreed to implement an equity transfer, with Party B acquiring 28.5% of the shares of Yuanxing Company from Party A, forming a new equity structure of Yuanxing Company, i.e., Party B holds 28.5% equity, Party A holds 11.5% equity, and Party C holds 60% equity; because Party A and Party C had a funding gap at the time of transferring the subject matter, in order to transfer all equity from the Property Exchange to Party A and Party C, Party B paid a lump sum of RMB 43 million on behalf of Party A as the consideration for Party B's acquisition of 28.5% equity, and this sum was secured by the equity of Party A and Party C as a pledge, and the original certificates of the relevant real estate project were delivered to Party B as another guarantee for performance; within three days after the completion of the transfer procedures, Parties A, B, and C shall sign a separate "Equity Transfer Agreement" and handle the equity modification procedures with the municipal industrial and commercial administrative department, and the said pledge shall be released simultaneously; Party A and Party C guarantee the legality and clear title of the company and the project land, and are responsible for all liabilities arising from disputes over the project land and title; Party A and Party C shall, after the completion of the equity transaction of Yuanxing Company, transfer the 28.5% equity held by Party A to Party B, and be responsible for registering the transfer of Party A's equity under Party B's name; Party A and Party C shall complete the overall equity modification procedures of Yuanxing Company within 20 days after signing this contract, to ensure that the equity transfer between Party A and Party B can be performed promptly; Parties A, B, and C shall complete all legal documents for this equity transfer in accordance with the agreement, and handle the equity modification procedures with the municipal industrial and commercial administrative department; Party B shall enjoy rights and assume corresponding obligations in accordance with the law and Yuanxing Company's articles of association, based on the proportion of equity it has acquired; if Party A and Party C fail to complete all legal procedures for Party B's equity transfer as agreed, it shall be deemed a default by Party A and Party C, and Party A shall unconditionally refund Party B's investment and pay liquidated damages of 1% per day of Party B's total capital contribution, and compensate Party B for all direct and indirect losses suffered as a result, while Party B's shares in the company held by Party A shall automatically revert to Party A; after Party B and Party C obtain a bank loan, based on the loan disbursement amount of RMB 100 million, the investment shall be repaid in proportion of 45% for Party B and 55% for Party C's shareholders, with the specific repayment amount being no less than RMB 30 million for Party A and no less than RMB 25 million for Party B, and the balance to be used for project development; after the project is completed and accepted, Party B shall share 11,000 square meters of building area at a unit cost of RMB 5,900 per square meter, including 2,000 square meters of commercial space and 9,000 square meters of office space; if either Party A or Party B fails to perform its agreed rights and obligations, it shall constitute a default, and the non-breaching party has the right to pursue the breaching party's liability, and the breaching party shall compensate the non-breaching party for all economic losses; if Party A, after the signing and implementation of this contract, fails to have Party B sign the share transfer agreement with Party A, Party B has the right to unilaterally terminate this contract and pursue economic liability against Party A and Party C; if Party B fails to invest the investment amount as agreed in this contract, Party A has the right to unilaterally terminate this contract and the share transfer agreement; disputes relating to the validity, performance, default, and termination of this contract shall be settled through friendly negotiation among the parties, and if negotiation fails, may be submitted to the people's court in the place where Party B is domiciled. The next day, the three parties signed a "Supplemental Agreement," stating: Since Party A had changed its enterprise name to Zhongxin Company in advance, the three parties confirmed that in the process of auction and equity transfer, all lawful rights and obligations shall be jointly and severally assumed by Party A and Zhongxin Company, and Zhongxin Company is added as Party G to the main contract; during the industrial and commercial registration process, after Zhongqian Company changed its name to Zhongxin Company, it shall exercise the rights and obligations of Party A. Zhongxin Company affixed its seal under Party G in the supplemental agreement to confirm. On the same day the supplemental agreement was signed, Zhongqian Company, Xianyuan Company, and Finance Company also signed a "Supplemental Agreement (Letter of Guarantee)" with Xiao Yutian, Liang Junxian, and He Shaoliu, stipulating that these three natural persons would serve as joint and several guarantors for the aforementioned equity transfer and project cooperation, assuming joint and several guarantee liability; if Zhongqian Company or Finance Company failed to perform all or part of the contract in a timely manner, Xianyuan Company had the right to require any one or more of these three persons to perform the obligation of repayment. After the signing of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" and the related supplemental agreements, they have not yet been submitted to the competent authority of foreign trade and economic cooperation of China for examination and approval.

On April 30, 2007, Xianyuan Company, by its own transfer or through the payment on its behalf by a third party, Guangdong Gaoxin Asset Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Gaoxin Company), transferred RMB 43 million to the Property Exchange supervision account designated by Zhongxin Company. On July 20, 2007, Zhongxin Company issued a receipt to Xianyuan Company, confirming receipt of Xianyuan Company's investment of RMB 43 million.

On June 4, 2007, the Yuexiu District Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation Bureau of Guangzhou, by Yue Wai Jing Mao Fu [2007] No. 103, approved the "Contract for Transfer of Capital Contributions and Interests" signed by Erqing Real Estate, Hong Kong Zhuokang, Zhongxin Company, and Finance Company, as well as the corresponding amendment to the cooperation contract and amendment to the articles of association of Yuanxing Company, to take effect. On July 24, 2007, the Guangzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a new business license to Yuanxing Company, and the cooperative parties (investors) of Yuanxing Company were changed from Erqing Real Estate and Hong Kong Zhuokang to Zhongxin Company and Finance Company; the legal representative and board members of the company were also changed accordingly.

After the completion of the said equity modification registration procedures, Zhongxin Company and Finance Company failed to transfer 28.5% of the 40% equity acquired by Zhongxin Company to Xianyuan Company's name as agreed in the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract." Xianyuan Company therefore, through Guangdong Shengchen Law Firm, sent a lawyer's letter to Zhongxin Company and Finance Company on August 23, 2007, asserting that the latter's actions constituted a breach of contract, demanding that they immediately proceed with the equity transfer procedures with Xianyuan Company, deliver the original certificates and licenses of the disputed real estate project to Xianyuan Company, and promptly advance the performance of the cooperation contract. On September 2, 2007, Zhongxin Company and Finance Company replied to Xianyuan Company, stating that the equity transfer stipulated in the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" faced certain legal obstacles, including: Yuanxing Company, as a Sino-foreign cooperative enterprise, was established with the foreign party providing registered capital and the Chinese party providing land use rights as cooperative conditions; the company's articles of association and approval documents did not stipulate or allocate equity (shares) among the cooperative parties in the company; therefore, the Chinese cooperative party was entitled to distribution rights of property after project completion but not equity; thus, in practice, it was impossible to transfer "equity" to Xianyuan Company, but only part of the property distribution rights after project completion; the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" did not specify the specific floors, directions, or orientation of the property that Xianyuan Company could share; in addition, the provisions regarding loans and distributions were unclear and lacked operability, and the sources of development funds were not clearly defined. However, Xianyuan Company believed that the contract was lawful, valid, and performable, and that Zhongxin Company and Finance Company should first handle the equity transfer procedures; therefore, it did not renegotiate the issues raised in the reply, and filed this lawsuit on September 24, 2007.

At the trial, all parties to the dispute agreed to apply mainland Chinese law as the governing law for the dispute. In addition, Xianyuan Company, Finance Company, and Yuanxing Company indicated that the approval procedures for the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" could be handled, while Zhongxin Company expressly stated that it would not assist in handling the approval procedures, on the ground that the contract was illegal and void, and that the owner of Zhongxin Company also disagreed with the cooperation method agreed upon. Xianyuan Company and Zhongxin Company both indicated that they did not agree to resolve the dispute by Zhongxin Company refunding the relevant equity transfer price and interest to Xianyuan Company.

With respect to the "original certificates and licenses of Yuanxing Company's real estate project" referred to in the third claim of this lawsuit, Xianyuan Company confirmed at trial that it referred to the original State-owned Land Use Certificate (No.: Sui Fu Guo Yong [2000] Zi Te No. 126) for the disputed real estate project, and asserted that the certificate was currently in the possession of Zhongxin Company; during the trial debate, Xianyuan Company indicated that it agreed that the original certificate could be placed in the custody of Lin Bang, the current legal representative of Yuanxing Company, or temporarily held by the Property Exchange. Relevant materials from the Property Exchange show that the certificate was transferred to the Property Exchange on February 2, 2007, received by Property Exchange staff member Gao Yongcai, and then transferred by Gao Yongcai to Zhongxin Company on August 13, 2007. The agent of Zhongxin Company stated at trial that he was unaware of this, and later replied in writing that Gao Yongcai had transferred the certificate to He Zuoyi, a director of Yuanxing Company. Investigation reveals that He Zuoyi is a director appointed by Zhongxin Company to Yuanxing Company.

The court of first instance additionally found: The original articles of association of Yuanxing Company recorded the cooperative parties as Erqing Real Estate (Party A) and Hong Kong Zhuokang (Party B). The registered capital of the company was USD 7.2 million, of which Party A provided the site and Party B contributed the registered capital of USD 7.2 million. Article 17 of the articles of association provided: "The board of directors shall consist of seven directors, of whom Party A shall appoint three and Party B shall appoint four. The term of office for directors shall be four years, and they may be re-appointed upon continued appointment by the appointing party." Article 18 provided: "The board of directors shall have one chairperson, appointed by Party A, and one vice chairperson, appointed by Party B." Article 42 provided: "After the building is completed, Party A and Party B shall each distribute 50% of the actual total floor area of the building (including the basement area)." Article 43 provided: "The distribution shall be made by dividing the entire building symmetrically along the north-south vertical centerline, with equal areas, with Party A allocated the northern portion and Party B allocated the southern portion." Article 65 provided: "The responsibility for liquidation of assets, claims, and debts, and the attribution and disposal of various equipment and facilities, shall be executed in accordance with the contract terms signed by both parties." After Zhongxin Company and Licai Company acquired the investment rights and interests in Yuanxing Company from Erqing Real Estate and Hong Kong Zhuokang, the articles of association of Yuanxing Company were amended accordingly, with Zhongxin Company as the cooperative Party A and Licai Company as the cooperative Party B. The registered capital of the company remained USD 7.2 million, with Party A providing the right to use land as a cooperative condition and Party B contributing USD 7.2 million in cash. Article 17 was amended to read: "The board of directors shall consist of three directors, of whom Party A shall appoint two and Party B shall appoint one. The term of office for directors shall be three years, and they may be re-appointed upon continued appointment by the appointing party." Article 18 was amended to read: "The board of directors shall have one chairperson, appointed by Party B." Article 42 was amended to read: "After the building is completed, Party A and Party B shall distribute the actual total floor area of the building (including the basement area) in a ratio of 4:6, with Party A receiving 40% and Party B receiving 60%." Article 43 was amended to read: "The distribution shall be made by dividing the entire building vertically along the north-south direction at a ratio of 6:4, with Party A allocated the northern portion and Party B allocated the southern portion." Article 65 was amended to read: "The responsibility for liquidation of assets, claims, and debts, and the attribution of property division, shall be executed in accordance with the relevant terms of the contract signed by both parties. The claims and debts of the cooperative company shall be borne by Party A and Party B in a ratio of 5:5 in accordance with the relevant laws and regulations of China concerning Sino-foreign cooperative joint ventures and the provisions of this contract."

During the proceedings of this case, Zhongxin Company also presented to the court of first instance the "Equity Transfer Agreement" dated January 9, 2007. This agreement was jointly signed by Erqing Real Estate, Hong Kong Zhuokang, Zhongxin Company, and Licai Company, with the matters agreed upon being substantially the same as the main content of the "Capital Contribution Amount and Rights Transfer Contract." Licai Company had no objection to the authenticity of this agreement but expressed that it was unclear why two contracts were signed for the same matter on the same day. Zhongxin Company submitted a written explanation to the court of first instance after the hearing, stating that when the "Capital Contribution Amount and Rights Transfer Contract" was signed on January 9, 2007, Zhongxin Company had not yet changed its name. The "Equity Transfer Agreement" was signed after the name change at the request of the Property Exchange, and the date was backdated to January 9, 2007, also at the request of the Property Exchange.

Furthermore, this case was initially accepted by the Tianhe District People's Court of Guangzhou. Based on the property preservation application and the guarantee provided by Xianyuan Company, the court issued a civil ruling (2007) Tian Fa Min San Chu Zi No. 8 on October 16, 2007, freezing Zhongxin Company's 28.5% shareholder equity in Yuanxing Company, and simultaneously sealing the house located at Room 3206, No. 39 Huaming Road, Tianhe District, Guangzhou, which was jointly owned by the guarantors Zhang Zhidong and Zhang Zhicheng.

The court of first instance held: Licai Company is a company registered in Hong Kong, so this case is a dispute over equity transfer involving Hong Kong and should be handled by analogy to foreign-related cases. The domiciles of Zhongxin Company and Yuanxing Company are both in Guangzhou. According to Article 22, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, which provides that "civil actions brought against legal persons or other organizations shall be under the jurisdiction of the people's court in the place of the defendant's domicile," this court, as the intermediate people's court with centralized jurisdiction over foreign-related civil and commercial cases in the place of the defendant's domicile, has jurisdiction over this case in accordance with the law. Since this case is a contract dispute and the parties at the hearing have unanimously agreed to apply the law of Mainland China, pursuant to Article 145, paragraph 1 of the General Principles of the Civil Law of the People's Republic of China and Article 4, paragraph 1 of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on the Application of Law in the Trial of Foreign-Related Civil or Commercial Contract Disputes, this court confirms that the law of Mainland China shall be the governing law for resolving the dispute in this case.

Based on the pleadings and arguments of both parties, the primary focus of the dispute in this case is the legal validity of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" signed by Zhongxin Company (using its former name Zhongqian Company at the time of contracting) with Xianyuan Company and Licai Company. Xianyuan Company, Licai Company, and Yuanxing Company all argued that the contract is valid, while Zhongxin Company claimed that the contract is void because it was not approved and violated the mandatory provisions of Mainland Chinese law. The court of first instance held that the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" reflected the true intentions of the contracting parties. Except for Article 5, paragraph 2, which provided that Xianyuan Company and Licai Company could directly recover part of their investment from the loan obtained for the disputed real estate project in proportion, which violated the mandatory provision of Article 36 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China that "after a company is established, shareholders shall not withdraw their capital contributions" and should therefore be void, the other provisions of the contract did not violate the mandatory provisions of Mainland Chinese laws or administrative regulations and should not be deemed invalid. Although Article 10 of the Sino-Foreign Cooperative Joint Venture Law of the People's Republic of China provides that "if one of the Chinese and foreign cooperative parties transfers all or part of its rights or obligations under the cooperative joint venture contract, it must obtain the consent of the other party and report to the examination and approval authority for approval," this only regulates the procedure for equity transfer and does not directly provide that foreign-related equity transfer contracts without approval are void. Moreover, there is no indication or evidence that upholding the validity of this contract would harm national interests or public interests. Therefore, it is not appropriate to deny the validity of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" under civil and commercial law based on the above legal provisions. More importantly, considering the background under which the parties signed the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract," this contract was entered into when Zhongxin Company and Licai Company were already preparing to acquire the equity of Yuanxing Company through an auction and had signed the "Capital Contribution Amount and Rights Transfer Contract" with the original investors of Yuanxing Company. However, due to a funding shortfall of RMB 45.918 million, the performance of the contract was facing difficulties. The timely advance of funds by Xianyuan Company prevented Zhongxin Company from defaulting and enabled it to successfully acquire 40% of the capital contribution rights and interests in Yuanxing Company. In this context, Xianyuan Company's good faith performance is commendable, and the contractual rights it enjoys accordingly should be protected by law. The court also noted that at the time the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" was signed, the "Capital Contribution Amount and Rights Transfer Contract" between Zhongxin Company, Licai Company, and the original investors of Yuanxing Company had not yet been approved by the examination and approval authority, and the equity of Yuanxing Company had not yet been transferred to Zhongxin Company's name. In such circumstances, it was impractical to require the parties to the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" to immediately submit the contract to the examination and approval authority for approval. If, solely because Zhongxin Company later changed its mind and refused to submit the contract for approval, the validity of the contract was denied, it would lead to a serious unfairness in the application of legal results. Additionally, from the content of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract," Xianyuan Company's obligation was to advance RMB 43 million in a lump sum as consideration for acquiring 28.5% of Zhongxin Company's equity, while the obligation to handle all legal procedures for the equity transfer, including transferring 28.5% of the 40% equity held by Zhongxin Company to Xianyuan Company's name, rested with Zhongxin Company and Licai Company. In other words, the approval procedure for the equity transfer was not a condition for the contract to take effect but rather a contractual obligation to be performed by one of the parties. Moreover, the equity transfer in this case was solely between Chinese parties, and there was generally no legal obstacle to approval. In summary, Zhongxin Company's defense that the contract is void lacks legal basis and is not adopted by this court. The "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" (except for Article 5, paragraph 2) is a contract legally established and is legally binding on the parties, and all parties shall comply with and execute it.

After the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" was signed, Xianyuan Company timely performed its obligation to pay the equity transfer consideration. However, after acquiring the equity of Yuanxing Company, Zhongxin Company delayed in transferring the portion due to Xianyuan Company to Xianyuan Company's name. Even during the hearing of this case, when Licai Company and Yuanxing Company both clearly indicated their willingness to cooperate in handling the equity transfer procedures, Zhongxin Company refused without justifiable reason to submit the contract to the examination and approval authority for approval. Its conduct constitutes malicious breach of contract and has objectively hindered the timely development and utilization of the land for the disputed real estate project. Zhongxin Company should bear corresponding civil liability. Now, Xianyuan Company's request for Zhongxin Company to immediately handle the equity transfer procedures and pay liquidated damages for delayed performance is in accordance with the law and is supported by this court. Yuanxing Company, as the cooperative enterprise, and Licai Company, as the foreign cooperative party, should also cooperate in handling the equity transfer procedures. As for the standard of liquidated damages, the contract stipulated 1% per day. Xianyuan Company, when filing the lawsuit, voluntarily adjusted it to 1‰ per day, which is a disposition of its litigation rights and should be respected in accordance with the law. According to Article 114, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, liquidated damages agreed upon only need to be appropriately reduced upon the request of a party if they are excessively high compared to the losses caused by the breach. In this case, Zhongxin Company's conduct clearly lacks good faith, and there is no evidence to prove that liquidated damages of 1‰ per day are excessively high compared to the losses suffered by Xianyuan Company due to Zhongxin Company's breach. Therefore, this court does not support Zhongxin Company's request to further reduce the liquidated damages standard from 1‰ per day. As for the original of the state-owned land use right certificate for the disputed real estate project, since it is originally owned by Yuanxing Company and holding the certificate is a necessary condition for Yuanxing Company to develop the disputed real estate project, and since Xianyuan Company stated at the hearing that it agreed to place the original certificate in the custody of Lin Bang representing Yuanxing Company or temporarily with the Property Exchange, this court respects the opinions of Xianyuan Company and Yuanxing Company. The relevant materials from the Property Exchange show that the original certificate has now been handed over to Zhongxin Company. Although Zhongxin Company responded that the recipient of the certificate was He Zuyi, a director of Yuanxing Company, since He Zuyi was a director appointed by Zhongxin Company, the responsibility for the handover of the certificate should still be borne by Zhongxin Company.

According to Article 10 of the Sino-Foreign Cooperative Joint Venture Law of the People's Republic of China, before handling the procedures for registration of the change in industrial and commercial registration for the equity transfer in this case, the parties involved should first go to the examination and approval authority to handle the relevant equity change procedures, including submitting the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" or an equity transfer agreement separately signed in accordance with that contract to the examination and approval authority for approval. According to the "Several Provisions on the Change of Investors' Equity in Enterprises with Foreign Investment" promulgated by the Ministry of Foreign Trade and Economic Cooperation and the State Administration for Industry and Commerce on May 28, 1997, when a Sino-foreign cooperative joint venture applies for approval and registration procedures for an equity change, it must submit legal documents such as the original contract and articles of association of the cooperative enterprise and their amendments, the board of directors' resolution on the investors' equity change, and the list of board members after the equity change. Therefore, during this process, the contracting parties should act in good faith, reasonably determine each other's rights and obligations through friendly negotiation in accordance with their respective equity ratios, and timely complete the relevant legal documents. If any party fails to cooperate, refuses to negotiate or sign the relevant legal documents, the other parties may, based on the equity structure agreed upon in the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" and on the basis of reasonably determining each party's rights and obligations, make corresponding amendments to the contract and articles of association of Yuanxing Company (for example, Zhongxin Company, Xianyuan Company, and Licai Company could respectively serve as Party A, Party B, and Party C of the cooperation; the registered capital of the company would remain USD 7.2 million; the capital contribution method would be that Parties A and B jointly provide the right to use land as a cooperative condition, and Party C contributes USD 7.2 million in cash; the board of directors could still consist of three directors, appointed respectively by Parties A, B, and C, with the chairperson appointed by Party C; the actual total floor area after the building is completed would be distributed in a ratio of 11.5% for Party A, 28.5% for Party B, and 60% for Party C; the distribution would be made by dividing the entire building vertically along the north-south direction at a ratio of 11.5:28.5:60, with Parties A, B, and C receiving portions from north to south in order; the claims and debts of Yuanxing Company would be borne by Parties A, B, and C in a ratio of 14.375:35.625:50 in accordance with relevant legal provisions and the principle of equal rights and obligations). The amended documents, resolutions, and the list of newly formed board members should then be submitted to the relevant authorities for approval and registration of the equity change.

As for the allocation of litigation costs, given that the dispute in this case arose from Zhongxin Company's lack of good faith, and Licai Company and Yuanxing Company had no fault in the performance of the contract, the litigation costs should be borne by Zhongxin Company in accordance with the law.

In summary, the court of first instance, in accordance with Article 22, paragraph 2 and Article 235 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 6, 8, 56, 60, and 107 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 10 of the Sino-Foreign Cooperative Joint Venture Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled as follows: 1. Zhongxin Company shall, within ten days from the date the judgment takes effect, submit to the examination and approval authority for approval the equity transfer matters under the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" jointly signed with Xianyuan Company and Licai Company; and within ten days from the date of approval by the examination and approval authority, go through the registration procedures for the change in equity with the administrative department for industry and commerce. Licai Company and Yuanxing Company shall cooperate in this regard. 2. Zhongxin Company shall, within ten days from the date the judgment takes effect, pay to Xianyuan Company liquidated damages up to the date the judgment takes effect (the liquidated damages shall be calculated based on Xianyuan Company's paid amount of RMB 43 million as the principal, at the rate of 1‰ per day, commencing from July 28, 2007; subsequent liquidated damages shall be calculated on the same principal and rate until the date the industrial and commercial registration procedures for the equity change are completed (the time for administrative approval and registration shall be deducted). Zhongxin Company shall pay the total amount in a lump sum on the date the industrial and commercial registration procedures for the equity change are completed. 3. Zhongxin Company shall, within ten days from the date the judgment takes effect, hand over the original of the state-owned land use right certificate numbered Suifu Guoyong (2000) Zi Te Di No. 126 to Lin Bang, the legal representative of Yuanxing Company, for safekeeping. The case acceptance fee for first instance of RMB 48,020 and the property preservation application fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Zhongxin Company.

Zhongxin Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the court of second instance, arguing that the judgment of first instance was unclear in fact finding, erroneous in application of law, and improper in result. It requested the revocation of the judgment of first instance, the dismissal of all claims of Xianyuan Company, and that the case acceptance fees for first and second instance be borne by Xianyuan Company.

The court of second instance additionally found the following facts:

On January 9, 2007, after Zhongxin Company and Licai Company respectively acquired 40% and 60% of the shares of Yuanxing Company from the original shareholders Erqing Real Estate and Hong Kong Zhuokang under the "Capital Contribution Amount and Rights Transfer Contract," according to the revised articles of association of Yuanxing Company, Zhongxin Company appointed He Shaoliu and He Zuyi as directors of Yuanxing Company, and Licai Company appointed Liang Junxian as chairman of Yuanxing Company. On July 24, 2007, Yuanxing Company obtained a new business license with Liang Junxian as the legal representative. On November 17, 2007, Yuanxing Company applied to the industrial and commercial department for a change of legal representative, changing the original legal representative Liang Junxian to Lin Bang. On January 14, 2008, the basic information on enterprise registration issued by the Guangzhou Administration for Industry and Commerce showed that the legal representative of Yuanxing Company was Lin Bang. During the first instance of this case, Lin Bang, as the legal representative of Yuanxing Company, entrusted lawyers Lu Jianjun and Wu Licai of Guangdong Xindesheng Law Firm as the entrusted agents of Yuanxing Company. The power of attorney bearing the official seal of Yuanxing Company showed the entrustment of lawyers Zhong Qi and Zhong Hua of Guangdong Hua'an United Law Firm as the entrusted agents of Yuanxing Company. The court of first instance recognized Lu Jianjun and Wu Licai as the lawful agents.

The court of second instance confirmed the other facts as found by the court of first instance.

The court of second instance held that this case is a dispute over a foreign-related equity transfer. According to Article 8(4) of the Supreme People's Court's Provisions on the Application of Law in the Trial of Foreign-Related Civil or Commercial Contract Disputes, which provides that "equity transfer contracts of Sino-foreign equity joint ventures, Sino-foreign cooperative joint ventures, and wholly foreign-owned enterprises" are subject to the laws of the People's Republic of China, this case should be governed by the laws of Mainland China. The court of first instance correctly applied the law, and the court of second instance affirms this.

The focus of dispute in the second instance is whether Zhongxin Company should, as agreed in the contract, transfer the 28.5% equity in Yuanxing Company it acquired from Erqing Real Estate to Xianyuan Company, bear liability for liquidated damages for failing to timely handle the equity transfer, and hand over the original of the state-owned land use right certificate to Lin Bang, the legal representative of Yuanxing Company, for safekeeping.

Regarding the issue of the qualifications of the entrusted agent of Yuanxing Company. After the legal representative of Yuanxing Company was changed from Liang Junxian to Lin Bang, Lin Bang, as the legal representative of Yuanxing Company, had the right to entrust an agent to participate in the litigation on behalf of Yuanxing Company. The court of first instance's recognition of Lin Bang's entrustment of lawyers Lu Jianjun and Wu Licai of Guangdong Xindesheng Law Firm as the entrusted agents of Yuanxing Company to participate in this litigation was not improper, and the court of second instance affirms this. Zhongxin Company's appeal argument that the court of first instance erred in denying the qualifications of lawyers Zhong Qi and Zhong Hua of Guangdong Hua'an United Law Firm as the entrusted agents of Yuanxing Company lacks sufficient basis, and the court of second instance does not support this argument.

Regarding the validity of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract." The parties to the contract have no objection to the finding of the first instance judgment that Article 5(2) of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" is an invalid clause, but have disputes over the validity of the contract. The facts of this case show that Yuanxing Company was a limited liability company in the nature of a Sino-foreign cooperative joint venture when it was established. On January 9, 2007, Zhongxin Company and Licai Company entered into the "Capital Contribution and Rights Transfer Contract" with the former shareholders of Yuanxing Company, Erfang Real Estate and Hong Kong Zhuokang, and respectively acquired 40% and 60% equity from the Chinese and foreign shareholders of Yuanxing Company. Thereafter, on April 28, 2007, Zhongxin Company, Licai Company, and Xianyuan Company entered into the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract," stipulating that Zhongxin Company would transfer 28.5% of the equity of Yuanxing Company it had acquired to Xianyuan Company. This is still an issue of equity transfer in a Sino-foreign cooperative joint venture. Pursuant to Article 10 of the "Sino-Foreign Cooperative Joint Venture Enterprise Law of the People's Republic of China," which provides that "If one party to a Chinese-foreign cooperative joint venture transfers all or part of its rights and obligations under the cooperative enterprise contract, it must obtain the consent of the other party and report to the examination and approval authority for approval," the further change of equity in Yuanxing Company should be examined and approved by the competent foreign investment authority of the state. According to Article 44(1) of the "Contract Law of the People's Republic of China," which provides that "A contract established in accordance with law shall become effective upon its establishment," and paragraph (2) thereof, which provides that "Where laws or administrative regulations stipulate that procedures such as approval or registration are required for the contract to become effective, such provisions shall prevail," the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" has not taken effect due to the failure to go through the approval procedures as required by law. However, the facts of this case show that the reason the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" did not take effect due to the failure to apply for approval was that, under the circumstances where Xianyuan Company, Licai Company, and Yuanxing Company were all willing to go through the approval procedures to facilitate the contract's entry into effect, Zhongxin Company expressly refused to cooperate with the other parties in completing the approval procedures to facilitate the contract's entry into effect. Zhongxin Company's act of intentionally causing the contract not to take effect objectively produced a similar legal effect as if the contract had taken effect. Therefore, with respect to the validity of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract," except for Article 5(2) which is an invalid clause, the contract was established in accordance with law but has not taken effect, yet it has legal binding force similar to that of an effective contract. Zhongxin Company appealed, arguing that the first instance judgment erred in determining the validity of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract." This claim lacks sufficient basis and is not supported by this court.

Regarding the issue of whether Zhongxin Company is obliged to transfer its 28.5% equity in Yuanxing Company to the name of Xianyuan Company. According to the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract," Zhongxin Company shall, within three days after completing the transfer of the equity it acquired in Yuanxing Company, go through the equity change procedures with Xianyuan Company and Licai Company at the administrative department for industry and commerce. On July 24, 2007, Zhongxin Company completed the equity transfer procedures and became one of the registered shareholders of Yuanxing Company. Zhongxin Company's compliance with the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" to complete the approval procedures for the equity transfer and transfer 28.5% of the equity of Yuanxing Company to Xianyuan Company is both a manifestation of compliance with the legal binding force of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" and a requirement of the principle of good faith in civil law. Viewed from the background of the execution of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract," Zhongxin Company had already acquired the equity of Yuanxing Company through auction and entered into the "Capital Contribution and Rights Transfer Contract" with the original contributors of Yuanxing Company. However, due to a funding gap of RMB 45.918 million, the performance of the contract encountered difficulties. Under these circumstances, Zhongxin Company reached an agreement with Xianyuan Company, obtaining a advance payment of RMB 43 million from Xianyuan Company in the form of transferring 28.5% of Yuanxing Company's equity to Xianyuan Company, thereby enabling Zhongxin Company to successfully acquire a 40% contribution rights in Yuanxing Company and avoid a breach of contract. Now, after utilizing Xianyuan Company's funds to acquire 40% equity in Yuanxing Company, Zhongxin Company refuses to transfer 28.5% of Yuanxing Company's equity to Xianyuan Company as agreed in the "Capital Contribution and Rights Transfer Contract" (should be "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract"), which is contrary to Article 4 of the "General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China," which provides that "Civil activities shall adhere to the principles of voluntariness, fairness, compensation for equal value, and good faith." Based on the above reasons, Xianyuan Company has the right to demand that Zhongxin Company facilitate the entry into effect of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" and request that Zhongxin Company complete the procedures for transferring 28.5% of Yuanxing Company's equity. There is reasonable basis for Zhongxin Company to transfer 28.5% equity of Yuanxing Company to Xianyuan Company in accordance with the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract." As for the issue that Zhongxin Company should cooperate with Xianyuan Company and Licai Company in going through the approval procedures of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract," this is covered by Xianyuan Company's claim that Zhongxin Company should transfer its 28.5% equity in Yuanxing Company to Xianyuan Company. The first instance judgment that Zhongxin Company should cooperate with Xianyuan Company and Licai Company in going through the approval procedures of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" was not improper. Zhongxin Company appealed, arguing that the first instance judgment requiring Zhongxin Company to cooperate with Xianyuan Company and Licai Company in going through the approval procedures of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" clearly exceeded Xianyuan Company's claims. This claim lacks sufficient basis and is not supported by this court.

Regarding the issue of Zhongxin Company paying liquidated damages to Xianyuan Company. According to the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract," if Zhongxin Company and Licai Company fail to complete the equity transfer procedures to Xianyuan Company as agreed, it shall be deemed a breach of contract, and Zhongxin Company shall refund Xianyuan Company's investment and bear liquidated damages calculated at 1% per day on the total amount of Xianyuan Company's capital contribution. The facts of this case show that Xianyuan Company advanced RMB 43 million, and Zhongxin Company acquired 40% equity of Yuanxing Company, but Zhongxin Company refused to cooperate in completing the procedures for transferring 28.5% equity to Xianyuan Company in accordance with the contract. Xianyuan Company has the right to claim liquidated damages from Zhongxin Company by reference to the contract. Xianyuan Company voluntarily reduced the liquidated damages standard to 1‰ per day, which is a manifestation of its exercise of the right of disposition, and this court supports it. The first instance judgment ordered Zhongxin Company to pay liquidated damages based on Xianyuan Company's contributed capital of RMB 43 million, calculated at 1‰ per day from July 28, 2007, which was not improper, and the second instance court affirms it. Zhongxin Company appealed, claiming that it did not breach the contract, and even if it did, the liquidated damages were too high. This claim lacks sufficient basis and is not supported by this court.

Regarding the issue of delivering the State-owned Land Use Right Certificate as a performance guarantee. According to the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract," Xianyuan Company advanced RMB 43 million on behalf of Zhongxin Company in a lump sum, and Xianyuan Company accepted the transfer of Zhongxin Company's 28.5% equity in Xianyuan Company (should be Yuanxing Company). The funds were secured by the equity pledge of Zhongxin Company and Licai Company, and the original copies of relevant documents and certificates for the real estate project were delivered to Xianyuan Company as another guarantee for performance. Xianyuan Company has the right to request Zhongxin Company to deliver the original copies of relevant real estate development documents and certificates to Xianyuan Company for safekeeping as a performance guarantee by Zhongxin Company. The facts of this case show that the original of the State-owned Land Use Right Certificate No. Suifu Guoyong (2000) Zi Te Di 126, which was disputed by the parties, was collected by He Zuoyi, a director appointed by Zhongxin Company to Yuanxing Company. Zhongxin Company should deliver the original of the [2000] Zi Te Di No. 126 State-owned Land Use Right Certificate to Xianyuan Company or a third party designated by Xianyuan Company for safekeeping. Xianyuan Company subsequently changed its request, asking Zhongxin Company to deliver the original of the State-owned Land Use Right Certificate to Lin Bang, the legal representative of Yuanxing Company, for safekeeping, which is a manifestation of Xianyuan Company's exercise of its civil rights, and this court supports it. The first instance judgment ordering Zhongxin Company to deliver the original of the [2000] Zi Te Di No. 126 State-owned Land Use Right Certificate to Lin Bang, the legal representative of Yuanxing Company, was not improper. Zhongxin Company appealed, arguing that the first instance judgment requiring Zhongxin Company to deliver the State-owned Land Use Right Certificate to Lin Bang, the legal representative of Yuanxing Company, for safekeeping exceeded Xianyuan Company's claim and constituted a procedural violation. This claim lacks sufficient basis and is not supported by this court.

In summary, the first instance judgment found the facts clearly, applied the law correctly, and the result was appropriate, and it should be upheld in accordance with law. Zhongxin Company's appeal lacks sufficient grounds and should be dismissed in accordance with law. The second instance court, pursuant to Article 153(1)(1) of the "Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China," ruled: dismiss the appeal and uphold the original judgment. The second instance case acceptance fee of RMB 48,020 is to be borne by Zhongxin Company.

Zhongxin Company, dissatisfied with the second instance judgment, applied to this court for retrial, arguing: (1) The "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" is essentially a loan contract, and the second instance judgment erroneously characterized it as an equity transfer dispute, which is a finding of basic facts lacking evidence. 1. From the background and purpose of the contract, the intent of signing the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" was to resolve the funding gap faced by Zhongxin Company and Licai Company during the auction by borrowing from Xianyuan Company, so as to complete the acquisition of Yuanxing Company's rights and interests. 2. Article 5(2) of the contract is not an agreement for Xianyuan Company to withdraw capital contributions, but is actually a guaranteed minimum return clause for Xianyuan Company to recover the loan, indicating that the contract is essentially a loan contract. 3. Article 2(1) of the "Security Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: "In economic activities such as lending, sales, transportation of goods, and processing and contracting, if creditors need to secure their claims by way of security, they may provide security in accordance with the provisions of this Law." This shows that the purpose of providing security is to guarantee the realization of claims, not to guarantee the realization of equity transfer. The "Supplementary Agreement (Letter of Guarantee)" stipulating that Xiao Yutian and others would assume joint and several guarantee liability for the performance of the contract also indicates that the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" is a loan contract. (2) If the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" is characterized as an equity transfer contract, it must be approved by the examination and approval authority to become effective; otherwise, it is invalid due to violation of mandatory legal provisions. The second instance judgment's determination that the contract was "established but not effective, yet has a legal binding force similar to an effective contract" is without basis. (3) Lin Bang used a fake seal to forge the application materials for change of registration and fraudulently obtained the status of legal representative of Yuanxing Company, and the agent he appointed cannot represent Yuanxing Company. The second instance judgment recognized the agent appointed by Lin Bang and erroneously found that "Yuanxing Company indicated that the approval procedures for the 'Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract' were feasible" and "Yuanxing Company agreed to deliver the land use right certificate to Lin Bang, the legal representative of Yuanxing Company, for safekeeping." (4) The second instance judgment's determination that Zhongxin Company must pay liquidated damages at 1‰ per day constitutes an incorrect application of law. Article 5(1) of the contract stipulates the liquidated damages for termination of the contract, and the parties did not agree on the standard for liquidated damages upon continued performance. Since no standard for liquidated damages upon continued performance was agreed, neither increasing nor decreasing the amount is justified. The second instance judgment's view that Xianyuan Company's voluntarily reduction of the standard to 1‰ per day at the time of filing the lawsuit was an exercise of its own litigation rights is also without basis. In summary, the second instance judgment found the basic facts without evidence, the main evidence for finding the facts was forged, and the application of law was erroneous. Requesting to set aside the second instance judgment, dismiss Xianyuan Company's claims; the litigation costs of this case shall be borne by Xianyuan Company.

Xianyuan Company responded: (1) The "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" is an equity transfer contract, not a loan contract. The parties never had the intent to borrow money. The contract clearly specifies the cause and effect of the equity transfer, the subject matter and price, and the procedures to be completed, and contains the essential terms of an equity transfer contract. There are no terms such as loan, interest, repayment period, etc., which should be included in a loan contract. The clause regarding the use of bank loans to repay the investment is an agreement made by the parties eager to recover their investment first, and has been ruled invalid by the court. This clause is also not a "guaranteed minimum return clause." Because Xianyuan Company paid RMB 43 million as consideration for the transfer, if it were a guaranteed minimum return clause in a loan contract, Xianyuan Company would recover the full amount, while Zhongxin Company would not have the right to recover its investment. Moreover, the clause also clearly states that the remaining bank loan will be used for project development. Furthermore, it is not only in loan relationships that debtors exist; in law, a debtor refers to a party who bears obligations in a specific rights and obligations relationship arising between parties. Guarantees are not limited to loan-related claims. Throughout the first and second instance proceedings, Licai Company and Yuanxing Company both confirmed that the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" is an equity transfer contract, not a loan contract, and the equity transfer was the genuine intention of all parties. (2) The lack of approval for the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" does not equate to invalidity. Zhongxin Company's claim of invalidity violates the principle of good faith. (3) The business registration materials of Yuanxing Company show that Lin Bang is the legal representative of Yuanxing Company. Lin Bang is the lawful person appointed by Licai Company to serve as director and chairman of Yuanxing Company in accordance with the company's articles of association, and has the authority to sign legal documents on behalf of Yuanxing Company. (4) The liquidated damages stipulated in the contract are for the breach of failing to complete the equity change registration procedures on time, and the choice to terminate the contract or demand continued performance is the right of the non-breaching party. Zhongxin Company's argument that liquidated damages apply only to the termination of the contract and refund of investment is sophistry. Therefore, the second instance judgment correctly found the facts and applied the law, and requests dismissal of Zhongxin Company's retrial application.

Yuanxing Company stated: In light of Liang Junxian's various actions, Licai Company revoked his director appointment in accordance with the articles of association and the law, and appointed Lin Bang as director and legal representative of Yuanxing Company, and went through the change procedures in accordance with the law, with formal registration at the industrial and commercial department. After Liang Junxian was aware of his replacement, he submitted a forged board resolution to the court. The seal of Licai Company on that resolution had long been obsolete, and Licai Company stated that it did not participate in any board meeting or pass any resolution. The findings of the two trial courts regarding the identity of Yuanxing Company's agent were correct. Zhongxin Company was hoping to acquire assets without putting up any capital, while Xianyuan Company had been actively participating in the operation of Yuanxing Company. The first and second instance judgments were correct, and requests dismissal of Zhongxin Company's retrial application.

Licai Company stated: During the process of participating in the Yuanxing Company project, Liang Junxian used fraudulent and improper means, causing serious damage to the rights and interests of the cooperative parties, and will be held accountable.

This court finds: Zhongxin Company claims that the basic facts found in the second instance judgment lacked evidence and that the main evidence for finding the facts was forged. However, from the specific grounds for applying for retrial, Zhongxin Company's objections to the second instance judgment's determinations regarding the nature of the contract, validity, agent qualification, and type of liquidated damages are essentially issues of legal characterization of the relevant matters. As to the facts found by the second instance judgment, Zhongxin Company has no substantive dispute. The other parties also raise no objection. Therefore, this court affirms the facts found by the second instance judgment.

This court holds: This case is a dispute over the transfer of equity (rights and interests) in a Sino-foreign (Hong Kong) cooperative joint venture. The second instance judgment applied Mainland law in accordance with the law, and neither party raises any objection. This court recognizes this.

The main issues in the review of this retrial are: the nature and validity of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract"; the qualification of the litigation agent of Yuanxing Company in the first and second instances; and whether Zhongxin Company should pay liquidated damages at Xianyuan Company's request.

(1) Regarding the nature of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract." The parties dispute whether the contract is an equity (rights and interests) transfer contract or a loan contract. The contract is titled "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract," and its content is that Xianyuan Company receives a transfer of 28.5% equity held by Zhongxin Company, the equity must be changed to the name of Xianyuan Company, and there are provisions on liability for breach if the equity change is not completed on time. Therefore, this contract is a typical equity (rights and interests) change contract. Zhongxin Company argues that, viewed from the background and purpose of the execution of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract," the contract is a loan contract. The contract was entered into against the background that Zhongxin Company faced a funding gap during the auction of Yuanxing Company's rights and interests, which is a fact. However, in real economic life, resolving funding difficulties through borrowing is not the only method; parties can also raise funds by transferring equity (rights and interests), among other means. In this case, the parties chose to raise funds by transferring equity (rights and interests), and there was no intention to borrow money. Zhongxin Company argues that Article 5(2) of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract" is a guaranteed minimum return clause, from which it can be inferred that the contract must be a loan contract. According to this clause, Zhongxin Company and Xianyuan Company would withdraw a portion of the loan obtained by Yuanxing Company to recover their investment first. This clause is a clause for early recovery of capital contributions, not a guaranteed minimum return clause, and certainly does not allow the entire contract to be characterized as a loan contract. Zhongxin Company argues that the provision of guarantees by others for the performance of the contract means the contract is a loan contract, which is a misunderstanding of the law. Article 2(1) of the "Security Law of the People's Republic of China" provides: "In economic activities such as lending, sales, transportation of goods, and processing and contracting, if creditors need to secure their claims by way of security, they may provide security in accordance with the provisions of this Law." This article only enumerates some situations where security is applicable, and it cannot be concluded that security can only be provided for lending, sales, transportation of goods, and processing and contracting. According to Article 89 of the "General Principles of Civil Law of the People's Republic of China," security may be provided for the performance of various types of debts. An equity (rights and interests) transfer contract is a kind of obligation in civil law, and providing security for its performance is in accordance with the law. Therefore, it cannot be concluded that the contract must be a loan contract simply because Xiao Yutian and others provided guarantees for the performance of the "Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract."

(2) Regarding the validity of the Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract. Article 10 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on Sino-Foreign Cooperative Joint Ventures provides: "If one party to a cooperative joint venture transfers all or part of its rights and obligations under the cooperative joint venture contract, it must obtain the consent of the other party(ies) and report to the examination and approval authority for approval." This Law does not explicitly specify the effect where such approval is not obtained. However, Article 44 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "A contract legally formed shall become effective upon its formation. Where a law or administrative regulation requires the contract to be subject to approval, registration, or other formalities for it to become effective, such provisions shall be followed." Pursuant to this Article of the Contract Law, although such a contract has been formed, unlike ordinary contracts that become effective upon formation, it is formed but has not yet become effective. The Supreme People's Court's Interpretation No. I on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides a clearer explanation of the effect of such contracts in its Article 9: "In accordance with the provisions of Article 44, paragraph 2 of the Contract Law, if a law or administrative regulation provides that a contract shall be subject to approval, or to approval, registration, or other formalities for it to become effective, and before the conclusion of the debate at the first instance trial, the parties have still not completed the approval formalities, or have still not completed the approval, registration, or other formalities, the people's court shall determine that the contract has not become effective." Therefore, the judgment of the second instance was correct in determining that the Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract was formed but had not become effective. Since the contract did not become effective due to the lack of approval, and the prerequisite for approval is that the party submits an application for approval, the obligation to submit an application for approval that would facilitate the contract becoming effective should arise at the time the contract is formed; otherwise, a party could maliciously prevent the contract from becoming effective by arbitrarily failing to perform or assist in performing the application formalities, which would clearly violate the principle of good faith. Article 8 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation No. II on Several Issues concerning the Application of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "After a contract that requires approval to become effective is formed, if one party who has the obligation to apply for approval fails to do so in accordance with the provisions of the law or the contract, this constitutes conduct that 'otherwise violates the principle of good faith' as referred to in Article 42, item (3) of the Contract Law, and the people's court may rule that the counterparty may handle the relevant formalities itself; the other party shall bear liability for damages for the expenses incurred and the actual losses caused to the counterparty." Given that the "counterparty" can handle the relevant formalities itself, and the "other party" shall compensate for the resulting losses, the "counterparty" can naturally also require the "other party" to handle the application for approval formalities. Therefore, the judgment of the second instance was correct in ordering Zhongxin Company to perform the obligation of submitting an application for approval to the examination and approval authority.

(3) Regarding the qualification of the agent. The legal representative of Yuanxing Company had been changed from Liang Junxian to Lin Bang. Zhongxin Company alleged that Lin Bang had obtained the status of legal representative of Yuanxing Company by fraudulent means, but provided no evidence; moreover, in the administrative lawsuit filed by former legal representative Liang Junxian of Yuanxing Company seeking revocation of the change registration, the court had dismissed his claim. Furthermore, according to Yuanxing Company's amended articles of association, the chairman of Yuanxing Company is appointed by Licai Company, and Licai Company never denied Lin Bang's status as the legal representative of Yuanxing Company in this litigation; on the contrary, it stated to this Court that it would pursue Liang Junxian's liability. Article 49 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "Citizens, legal persons, and other organizations may serve as parties to civil litigation. A legal person shall participate in litigation through its legal representative." In accordance with the above legal provisions, the litigation agent authorized by Lin Bang, the legal representative of Yuanxing Company, by signing the power of attorney, has the authority to represent Yuanxing Company in litigation, and the statements made by the relevant litigation agent during the litigation phase are binding on Yuanxing Company. The judgment of the second instance, based on the opinion of Yuanxing Company's litigation agent, correctly determined that Yuanxing Company indicated that the approval formalities for the Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract could be handled and that Yuanxing Company agreed to place the land use right certificate in the custody of Lin Bang, the legal representative of Yuanxing Company.

(4) Regarding liquidated damages. Article 5, paragraph 1 of the Equity Transfer and Project Cooperation Contract provides: If Zhongxin Company and Licai Company fail to complete all legal formalities for the equity transfer as agreed, this shall be deemed a breach, and Zhongxin Company shall unconditionally refund Xianyuan Company's investment funds and bear liquidated damages at a rate of 1% per day of the total invested amount. Zhongxin Company's assertion that this clause only stipulates liquidated damages for termination of the contract reflects a misunderstanding. According to this breach of contract liability clause, as long as Zhongxin Company breaches the contract, it must pay liquidated damages at 1% per day, and Xianyuan Company may also demand termination of the contract. Whether to choose termination of the contract or to demand continued performance of the contract is Xianyuan Company's statutory right. When filing the lawsuit, Xianyuan Company voluntarily reduced the liquidated damages rate to 1‰ per day, which is a disposition of its own rights and does not violate the principle of party autonomy. Therefore, the judgment of the second instance correctly ordered Zhongxin Company to pay liquidated damages to Xianyuan Company at the rate of 1‰ per day.

In summary, the grounds for the application for retrial by Guangdong Zhongda Zhongxin Investment Planning Co., Ltd. (Zhongxin Company) are untenable, and its application does not meet the circumstances set forth in Article 179, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China. Pursuant to Article 181, paragraph 1 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the ruling is as follows:

The application for retrial by Guangdong Zhongda Zhongxin Investment Planning Co., Ltd. is rejected.
